6	# Parallell session support
7	
8	## Goal
9	A person working with KiwiAgent rarely works with KiwiAgent alone: a second plan or implement session runs beside the first, and an agent outside KiwiAgent, a branch switch or the person's own editor changes the same files. Today the agent cannot tell its own work from anyone else's, so it writes over a change it never saw and, worse, verification blames the feature for tests the other hand broke. This feature gives the agent that distinction: every change in the workspace is either this session's own or another hand's, a write onto a file another hand moved is refused instead of instructed against, a running session is told when the ground shifts under it, and a failing test in code the feature never touched is reported as someone else's rather than handed back to the implementer.
10	
11	## Writing a file another hand changed
12	Every session that writes — plan, implement, cleanup, chat — is held to the same check, which the extension performs rather than the prompt asking for it.
13	- **Stale write refused**: a write to a file whose content changed since this session last saw it is refused, and the refusal says what changed the file (docs/intent/agent.md#Verification).
14	  - **Own writes are seeing**: a write the session itself made counts as seeing the file, so two edits in a row to the same file are never refused.
15	  - **Folded read is not seeing**: a read the conversation no longer holds after compaction is not seeing the file, so a write after it is refused until the file is read again (docs/features/own-loop-compaction.md#Reading again before writing).
16	- **Unread file refused**: a write to a file that exists and this session never read is refused for the same reason.
17	  - **A new file needs no read**: writing a file that does not exist is not refused.
18	- **No read-before-edit instruction**: the phase instructions carry no rule telling the model to read before editing, because the refusal enforces it (docs/intent/agent.md#Instructions).
19	- **Who changed it**: a refusal or notice names the other KiwiAgent session and the feature it works on where the change came from one, and otherwise says the change came from outside KiwiAgent, without naming which tool (docs/features/coordination.md#Claims).
20	
21	## Being told while the work is in play
22	- **Notice of another hand**: a session whose turn is in play is told, as a one-line tail on its next tool result, that another hand changed a file this session has written or read (docs/features/coordination.md#Channels).
23	  - **One notice per file**: a file is reported once until this session sees it again, and a change sweeping many files at once is reported as a single line naming the count rather than one line per file.
24	- **The task's work is its own**: the files a task names as touched are the ones its own runs wrote, and a foreign change to one of them is recorded on the task instead of counted as the task's work (docs/intent/agent.md#Phase 3: Implement).
25	
26	## A verification failure that is not ours
27	Verification is mechanical and runs over the files the tasks name; with a second hand in the workspace, some of what fails there was never this feature's doing.
28	- **Foreign failure**: a failing test whose file no session of this feature wrote, and which another hand changed since this feature's implementation began, is recorded as foreign and not handed to the implementer (docs/intent/agent.md#Verification).
29	  - **Narrowed to the function**: where a file's changes can be attributed function by function, a failing test whose own function another hand changed is foreign even though this feature wrote other parts of that file.
30	  - **No other hand no excuse**: when nothing changed outside this feature's own sessions since its implementation began, every failure is the feature's and is handed to the implementer as before.
31	- **Retry before asking**: a verification run whose failures are all foreign waits a configured number of seconds and runs the same suites again, and only a second all-foreign failure is reported (docs/settings.md#Settings).
32	  - **Ours on the second run**: a failure that is the feature's own on the retry is handed to the implementer like any other failure.
33	- **Held rather than verified**: a feature whose verification ends in foreign failures stays in verification with the failures recorded on the board, naming the files and the hand, and the user is asked whether to run again, hand them to the implementer anyway, or accept them (docs/intent/agent.md#Stages).
34	- **Budget spared**: an all-foreign failure does not count against `kiwiAgent.verifyFailureBudget` (docs/intent/agent.md#Verification).
35	
36	## Open questions
37	- **Verifying beside a live sibling**: should verification be postponed while another KiwiAgent session in the same workspace is mid-turn, rather than run and then be retried?

130	### The check has no voice
131	
132	The check has no conversation of its own: while it works, the person sees a single line of progress on the plan it runs under. What it cannot settle it writes down as a finding for the person to rule on, and never asks.
133	
134	## Retrieval
135	
136	A sub-session the planner calls with `retrieve(question, known, budget)` to keep file dumps out of its own context. Phase 2 first; phase 1 only when the intent tree or work-item graph outgrows the planner.
137	
138	- Locates and quotes, never interprets. Output is verbatim excerpts with provenance; the planner rules on them. A summary drops nuance silently, and the planner never sees what was left out.
139	- Tools are derived, not configured: the calling phase's tool set minus AskUserQuestion and anything that writes. Phase 1 retrieval is blind by construction.
140	- No user interaction, no recursion. "Needs X to answer" goes in `not_found`; the planner decides whether to ask. Depth 1.
141	- Result: `findings[]` (excerpt, source as `path#heading`, work item id or URL, one line on why it matches), `not_found[]` (what was looked for, where), `status: complete | partial | budget_exhausted`. Partial is a result, not an error.
142	- Written to `.agent/runs/<id>/retrieval/<n>.md`; the tool returns path, status and counts. Files on disk, not conversation context.
143	- Budget per call (tool calls, tokens), set by the planner. Exhaustion returns findings so far.
144	- Runs as a `CodeSession` under its own profile; a cheap model is fine because the task is search.
145	- Independent questions fan out as independent sessions, no shared state.
146	
147	## Phase 3: Implement
148	
149	Tools: Read, Write, Edit, Glob, Grep, JsonSchema, JsonQuery, MarkdownSearch, Bash, ReadTasks, UpdateTask. Input is the approved spec and its task board; refuses to start on `status: draft` or without a tasks file. One run per task, under the plan's tab, started by the extension on the next unfinished task and closed once that task is tested or blocked, when the next one's run starts. A run starts on its task in full, the text of the rules it delivers and what earlier tasks built, so it never inherits a context filled with finished work, and its system prompt is the same for every task, so each run after the first starts on a cached prefix. A task whose run stopped unfinished is carried on by that run. A failed test sweep goes to a fix run of its own, started on the failure and the tasks it names. A decision ruled `keep` reaches it in the kickoff of the task that delivers a rule the decision is `on`: the spec stands, the code changes. A fork the spec and the code leave open is put to the user with AskUser and the run carries on with the answer. An answer on a rule the task delivers amends the spec under the contract, and the board is derived again when the run's turn ends, without a check: the run has read the code. An answer that reaches further is an unfiled decision. Writes go through the ordinary permission prompt; no scope guard. An implement session may write anywhere the user allows, generated files included: what protects generated output is that the next build rewrites it wholesale, so an edit into it is lost, not refused.
150	
151	- Task state is the board, read with `ReadTasks` and moved with `UpdateTask`: the extension marks a task in progress when its run starts, and the run records how it ended, tested when every rule the task delivers is proven by a passing test, blocked with a reason when it cannot finish, done when it must stop with the code written but untested. A tested task says what it `built`, by name and file: the hand-off the tasks after it start from. The task names every file it touched: the sweep runs over them, so tested is refused on a task that names none. The board file itself is denied to the implementer's Write and Edit.
152	- Coverage is the evidence: the task's proofs name, per delivered rule, the test file and the test whose name states the rule. The plan view shows on each rule and edge case which task delivers it and which test proves it, or `no task` / `no test`; a task marked tested with a rule it names no test for is flagged. That is what an acceptance section used to promise, made checkable.
153	- Only tested is a finish. A board whose every task is tested goes to verification; the plan bar stops offering Implement, since a second session would re-read the code and decide for itself what to redo. Blocked is unfinished work, so it still takes a fresh session. The feature's state is derived from the task states, not a `status` of its own: adding a task to a finished board makes it unfinished again with nothing to reset, and the two can never disagree.
154	
155	## Unfiled decisions
156	
157	A decision the user makes outside planning, one a blind planner could otherwise decide differently, is intent the planner cannot see. The session that hears it records it where the planner reads. Within the task being built, it amends the spec. Reaching further, from an implement run, a plan session or a chat, it becomes an entry in `plan/unfiled-decisions.md`: committed, readable in phase 1, and outweighing a doc or spec that says otherwise. Written in the product's language, never a path or a symbol. *File decisions* is a session with the planner's read scope that moves each entry into the specs and docs it names, each write confirmed, and deletes it once filed; an implemented spec is not amended, since the change is a feature to plan. The pick-up menu shows how many entries wait.
158	
159	## Migration
160	
161	`KiwiAgent: Migrate plans` brings every plan under `plan/` to the contract; Repair in the plan bar does it for one. By rule first: a markdown task board becomes the JSON one (the extension also does this for every board when it starts), a legacy `## Tasks` section becomes the board (delivered rules first, state kept), a `## Decisions` section or a findings table becomes the decisions file (a table's rows titled by their ids), id-shaped lines in every file become the named shapes with the old id standing in as the name, the board is stamped. What remains (invariants, acceptance criteria, flat edge cases, rules still named by an id) goes to the plan session as a prompt: group into scenarios, nest edges, fold restated rules, give each rule a real name, and mark one that survives under a new name with `(was I3)`. When that turn ends the extension follows each rename through the review targets, the tasks' delivered rules and the decisions, drops the notes and stamps the board. Approval is kept on a migrated approved spec: the arrangement changed, not the rules.
162	
163	## Verification
164	
165	Mechanical, no model: once every task is tested, the extension runs the `kiwiAgent.verify` rules over the files the tasks name. A rule is a file glob, a project marker and a command (`**/*.cs` with `*.csproj` runs `dotnet test` in that project; `src/**/*.ts` with `package.json` runs `npm test` there), so a feature that touched only the backend runs only the backend's tests, and a repo with a backend and a frontend bundle runs each once. The outcome is recorded on the board, newest first; the output tail goes to the run log. A failure is handed to the implement session (the live one for the feature, or a fresh one) with the command and its output; the run repeats when the board is all tested again, up to `kiwiAgent.verifyFailureBudget` consecutive failures, after which the failed record stays for the user. Verify again is offered from the plan bar.
166	
167	Parked: build scoped to the project owning the edited file; read-before-edit staleness enforced in a hook rather than by prompt.
168

5	## Claims
6	
7	- Registry `.agent/sessions/<session id>.json`: session id, mode, `plan_item_id`, claimed files, `deadline` (set by the session from the item's scope), last heartbeat.
8	- A PreToolUse hook on Edit and Write claims the file on first touch. If another live session holds it, the edit is denied and the message names that session and its plan item.
9	- A session reports an item done through the task-state tool, which releases its claims.
10	- Silence past `deadline` flags the claim as stale in the Sessions view and on the tab (status `needs_human`). Nothing is released automatically.
11	- Force-release from the Sessions view posts a revocation message into the stale session: it stops immediately, does not finish the in-flight edit, reports the files it touched, and its claims are removed.
12	
13	## Checkpoints
14	
15	- Tools `checkpoint(reason)` and `revert(checkpoint)` in implement sessions, opt-in per call.
16	- A checkpoint copies the current content of the files the session holds claims on into `.agent/runs/<id>/checkpoints/<n>/`, with the reason.
17	- `revert` compares each file's hash with the one recorded at checkpoint time and refuses files that changed underneath; the rest are restored. No git involvement.
18	- Checkpoint reasons are listed in the transcript; more than three on one plan item marks the item for review in the plan bar.
19	
20	## Channels
21	
22	- `send(session, text)` returns immediately. The receiver sees a one-line "1 message waiting" tail on its next tool result and pulls the text with `read_messages()`, which returns it as a tool result.
23	- The tail repeats until the queue is drained. A session that has stopped calling tools gets the message as its next user turn instead.
24	- Threads are capped at a configurable length; beyond it the next message is refused and the user is notified in the Sessions view.
25	
26	Not included: shared memory between sessions, automatic conflict resolution, cross-workspace sessions.
